title: 3. Saltzer & Schroeder — 8 Design Principles
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L06: Security Principles & Mindset: 3. Saltzer & Schroeder — 8 Design Principles .

blocks.text: The Classical 8 (1975, still canonical 50 years later)

rows: KISS — smaller designs have fewer bugs
Default deny; access requires explicit permission
Check authority on every access, no caching of decisions
Security must not depend on secrecy of the algorithm (Kerckhoffs)
Minimum access required to do the job
Security must be usable or it will be bypassed

blocks.text: Security teams that argue against "complete mediation" usually call it "performance optimization." The principle is older than the internet — and still wins arguments.

items: Complete Mediation → Zero Trust ("never trust, always verify")
Fail-Safe Defaults → AWS IAM deny-by-default policy
Open Design → AES, TLS, OpenSSH all public algorithms
Psychological Acceptability → if MFA takes 90 seconds, users disable it
Least Privilege → reduces blast radius from compromised credentials

cheatsheet: Economy of Mechanism: KISS — smaller designs have fewer bugs
Fail-Safe Defaults: Default deny; access requires explicit permission
Complete Mediation: Check authority on every access, no caching of decisions
Open Design: Security must not depend on secrecy of the algorithm (Kerckhoffs)
Separation of Privilege: Multi-key locks — two-person control
Least Privilege: Minimum access required to do the job
Least Common Mechanism: Minimize shared resources between subjects
Psychological Acceptability: Security must be usable or it will be bypassed
